dateline: Washington / Brussels / Bucharest / Helsingborg / Warsaw / Stockholm — 2017–2026
heroHeadline: HELSINGBORG T-6: CNN CONFIRMS 10,200+ US TROOP CUTS ACROSS EUROPE; B9 BUCHAREST 'NATO 3.0' DECLARATION ADOPTED; RUTTE 0.25% GDP UKRAINE PLEDGE ($143B/YEAR) ON AGENDA; NATO EVENT PROGRAMME PUBLISHED
heroSubtitle: On May 14, 2026, CNN published a comprehensive breakdown confirming that Trump's European troop cuts total 10,200+ soldiers: the Germany 5,000 withdrawal (in process) plus the cancelled 4,700-troop 2nd ABCT Poland rotation and a 500-soldier rocket/missile battalion. The cumulative reduction to ~70,000 would breach NDAA §1249's 76,000 statutory floor without congressional authorization — a constitutional conflict the White House has not acknowledged. CFR analysts note the missile cancellations (following the May 5 Tomahawk/hypersonic cancellation) represent a larger strategic deterrence retreat than the troop numbers suggest. On May 13, NATO Secretary General Rutte attended the B9 + Nordic Allies Summit in Bucharest with Presidents Dan (Romania), Nawrocki (Poland), Zelensky (Ukraine), and B9/Nordic delegations. The joint declaration designated Russia 'the most significant and direct long-term threat' and implicitly framed the alliance's evolution as 'NATO 3.0': European allies assume primary responsibility for conventional defense; US provides nuclear deterrence and intelligence backstop — the first formal multi-nation document to codify the structural recalibration. Rutte proposed a binding 0.25% GDP/year Ukraine military pledge for all 32 allies (~$143B/year total), to be debated at Helsingborg (May 21–22) and formalized at Ankara (July 7–8). May 15 is T-6 before the Helsingborg emergency Foreign Ministers Meeting — NATO published the full event programme confirming four agenda clusters: Ukraine support sustainability, defense spending acceleration (Poland pushing 5% GDP by 2030), eastern flank reshuffle post-US cuts, and alliance governance reform (Rasmussen coalition of willing). Southern ally resistance to the Ukraine pledge noted. Background arc: May 12 — EU FAC Defence (Kallas: 'red lines'); May 11 — Rutte-Sybiha NATO HQ; May 10 — formal contingency planning; May 9 — Rasmussen 'disintegrating'; May 7 — 'terror incubators'; May 1 — 5,000 from Germany. Next: Helsingborg FMM May 21–22; Ankara Leaders' Summit July 7–8, 2026.
